text.name: Looks like you got mom
text.text:
Police: It seems you received your mother's call.
Police: She should have told you everything, right? Are you going to come to the police station with her?
Respondent: He has never believed in God.
Respondent: He said that no matter how deep you dig, a shovel can never smell the scent of the soil.
Respondent: When the child was so seriously ill before, he never prayed for her even once.
Respondent: So he is simply unwilling to believe.
Respondent: Thanks to my day and night prayers, we received God's grace.
Respondent: He always gets angry at himself for not having the ability to change all of this.
Respondent: Did he really... turn himself in?
Respondent: If it really was him who took her, it might be because of the child support issue. Since the middle of last year, he mentioned it to me several times.
Respondent: He said he was short on money and truly couldn’t come up with the child support.
Respondent: I told him this stage is crucial for the child. I told him to pull himself together as soon as possible. No matter what, Xiyuan is still his child.
Respondent: But he just wouldn’t pray,
Respondent: and still wanted to rely on his own strength to change everything.

text.name: You called Siwon’s dad
text.text:
Police: Did you call Xiyuan’s father?
Respondent: I’ve already called him several times, but he still hasn’t answered.
Respondent: We only see each other once a year on Xiyuan’s birthday. We basically don’t keep in touch otherwise.
Respondent: Honestly, it’s one thing not to answer calls usually, but how can he not answer my call at a time like this!
Respondent: Actually, on the day the police came to our home, I sent him a text message.
Respondent: It was the first time the child told me she missed her dad.
Respondent: Then I told him that Xiyuan missed him and asked if he could come see the child.
Respondent: But how could he be so cold-hearted...

text.name: Hello, you’re Siwon’s
text.text:
Police: Hello, are you Xiyuan’s mother? I’m Quan Jing from Huaming Police Station.
Police: May I see Xiyuan?
Respondent: Oh my!
Respondent: I thought it was a delivery and it startled me. Next time if you come over for something, could you not ring the doorbell? You can just knock. The child is sleeping—I’m afraid of waking her up.
Respondent: I was about to cook, but she started dozing off while watching TV, so I coaxed her to sleep.
Respondent: Come in. She’s under the blanket—I’m not sure if you can see her clearly.
Respondent: Yesterday I took Xiyuan out for a long walk. Maybe she got tired. She had just woken up not long ago and is already sleepy again...
Respondent: Children grow very fast. Xiyuan suddenly grew taller too. There isn’t a single piece of clothing at home that fits her, so I took her out to buy some clothes and things. There’s so much to prepare before school starts, and we still need to have the school uniform tailored. I don’t know when this child will wake up to eat...
Respondent: If you want to see Xiyuan, you’ll probably have to wait a while.
Respondent: By the way...
Respondent: What do you need to see Xiyuan for?

text.name: You went to the playground to look
text.text:
Police: When you went to the amusement park to look for Xiyuan, did you see a boy who looked like this?
Respondent: Do you know the stationery store next to the amusement park?
Respondent: A few days ago... after that boy came out of the amusement park, he went to that stationery store.
Respondent: At that time, the boy was playing with Xiyuan, so when he ran out, I watched him for a while.
Respondent: Why are you suddenly asking about this? Is he related to Xiyuan’s disappearance?

text.name: Do you really think it was
text.text:
Police: Do you really think Mr. Jin Kangshi took the child away?
Respondent: Well:
Respondent: Was it really him? Do you think he did it? No matter what, that’s not his personality.
Respondent: There is someone else...
Respondent: Officer Quan, I’m not trying to clear Jin Kangshi of suspicion. I just want to tell you what I saw.
Respondent: There is a woman who often wanders around near that amusement park.
Respondent: Whenever I went to look for Xiyuan, I would see her every time I passed by there.
Respondent: She looks to be in her thirties or forties, and she’s quite tall... probably about 10 centimeters taller than me.
Respondent: That woman often stares toward the amusement park.
Respondent: The place where she stands is a little distance from the amusement park, and there are flowers blocking the view, so she’s not easily noticed. But if someone is tall enough, they can see the amusement park from there.
Respondent: That woman often stands there on tiptoe, looking past the flower bed.
Respondent: ...By the way, Officer Quan.
Respondent: What is the name of the child Kangshi took away?

text.name: I’m coming right now.
text.text:
Police: I’m on my way right now. Keep talking and don’t hang up. What happened?
Respondent: My mom called me.
Respondent: Xiyuan’s grandmother—she said she was at the supermarket in front of the residential complex, but the security guard called saying the fire alarm in her home went off.
Respondent: The security guard was worried there was a fire and was going to check her home, but he couldn’t open the door. My mom wanted me to go over and help open it.
Respondent: I told her I couldn’t leave Xiyuan alone and asked her to hurry back herself.
Respondent: But she insisted that I go...
Respondent: She said she would arrive soon and would pick up the child at the amusement park, and told me to go upstairs to take a look and then come right back down.
Respondent: She said the timing would be just right, and that she would wait downstairs with the child.
Respondent: I went to my mom’s home and found the security guard indeed waiting at the door, so I opened it. I don’t know what she left in the pot, but when we went in, it had already burned dry and the room was filled with smoke.
Respondent: The security guard helped turn off the gas and open the windows for ventilation.
Respondent: At that moment, I was thinking how lucky it was that I hadn’t brought the child upstairs. Otherwise, breathing in so much smoke would definitely be bad for her health. Fortunately, the house didn’t catch fire... Then I hurriedly took the elevator down.
Respondent: It was only a few minutes, but...
Respondent: When I came down, my mom was indeed standing downstairs as we had agreed.
Respondent: I asked her where Xiyuan was.
Respondent: She told me, wasn’t Xiyuan taken upstairs by you?
Respondent: Officer Quan, when will you arrive?

text.name: Calm down first.
text.text:
Police: Calm down first. Speak slowly. Who are you?
Respondent: Officer! Is it Officer Quan?
Respondent: Do you remember me?
Respondent: That day you came to our home to look for Xiyuan, remember? I even told you not to ring the doorbell... Do you remember now?
Respondent: Officer Quan, what should I do...
Respondent: Please come quickly...
Respondent: Xiyuan...
Respondent: Xiyuan is missing! At the amusement park.

text.name: Enrollment notice recei
text.text:
Police: Did you receive the admission notice? I heard you didn’t go to register.
Police: I came to investigate the situation. Times are not like before. Just consider it as me being nosy.
Police: The subdistrict office said they have already spoken with Xiyuan’s grandmother on the phone, but I still think it’s better to come and communicate face to face.
Police: Is Xiyuan doing well?
Respondent: Of course.
Respondent: Do you visit every household in person? That must be very hard.
Respondent: You’ll see in a moment. She’s very healthy now and is completely ready to attend school.
Respondent: After staying in the hospital for so long, it’s amazing that she’s still so lively and cheerful.
Respondent: Her personality might be inherited from her father. She already made people worry when she was still in my womb.
Respondent: Oh, I haven’t told you, right? Our Xiyuan was born prematurely at seven months.
Respondent: Every time the doctor saw me, he would scare me, saying she might have this or that problem, and handed me a stack of consent forms to sign.
Respondent: But I always believed that she would pull through and tightly grasp me with her little hands.
Respondent: If you’re worried that we’re abusing the child or something, that’s completely unnecessary.
Respondent: Although Xiyuan’s father and I are not living together now, her grandmother and I take good care of her.
Respondent: We will definitely attend the school opening ceremony.
Respondent: Thank you for caring about us so much.
Respondent: The meal seems to be ready. Would you like to eat before you leave?

text.name: Did Siwon ever
text.text:
Police: Has Xiyuan ever gone somewhere else alone before?
Respondent: ...Do you think... that’s possible?
Respondent: Officer Quan... I think...
Respondent: Xiyuan might have disappeared because of me.
Respondent: Ever since I had surgery when giving birth to Xiyuan, my health hasn’t been very good, and I stayed in the hospital for a long time.
Respondent: Because I was lying in a hospital bed myself, I couldn’t stay by her side to take care of her.
Respondent: She grew up looking at the hospital ceiling. I thought I could understand her, since I had a similar experience.
Respondent: But... Xiyuan’s thoughts might be different from mine.
Respondent: Do you think Xiyuan resents me in her heart?
Respondent: She doesn’t even call me mom anymore.
Respondent: She often runs out and doesn’t come back. I had to go to several amusement parks before I found her...

text.name: The afternoon of February 3
text.text:
Police: Who was the person you spoke with on the afternoon of February 3?
Respondent: As you can see, we don’t have many permanent staff in our office, so I basically handle all the phone calls myself.
Respondent: Are you referring to Ms. Shen Huijing? The afternoon of the 3rd?
Respondent: We generally don’t make calls during working hours, for fear that they might have opinions and think we are monitoring their work... And it’s even less likely that we would call her in the afternoon.
Respondent: Ah, we did make one call. There was nothing particularly important.
Respondent: In a few days, there will be a Best Housekeeping Service Worker Commendation Conference.
Respondent: I called to ask if she could come and attend. There are over 100 housekeeping service workers registered with us, but not a single one is willing to come.
Respondent: But after the call, I regretted it. She definitely won’t come.
Respondent: Ms. Shen Huijing, you’ve probably met her too, right? After saying just a few words, she hangs up. She’s busy taking care of the child every day and hasn’t shown up at the office for a long time.
Respondent: Why are you looking for her?
Respondent: As long as we don’t receive complaints, it’s fine, but when the police come, it’s a bit...
Respondent: Besides, she’s not the type to slack off while working:

text.name: Nanny Employment Proof
text.text:
Nanny Employment Certificate
Employee: Shen Huijing / Born February 6, 1976 / Female
Employer: Cui Dongjian / Born September 15, 1972 / Male
This is to certify that the above employer has employed the above employee as a nanny from July 1, 2009 to the present.
February 4, 2012
Love Crystal Housekeeping Service Center

text.name: Is this the subdistrict office
text.text:
Police: Is this the subdistrict office?
Respondent: Yes, Captain. Work must be tough, right?
Respondent: I am the director of Rongzhou Subdistrict Office.
Respondent: Here’s the situation: for this year’s new student registration, there are four children in our subdistrict who have not registered.
Respondent: I’m calling mainly to ask for your help.
Respondent: I’ve already spoken with the parents of these four children on the phone. Some said they went abroad for travel, and some said they were too busy with work.
Respondent: The elementary school opening ceremony hasn’t started yet, so I have reported to my superiors that there is no problem.
Respondent: Although it has been confirmed, the process still needs to be followed.
Respondent: The official letter requesting assistance is currently under approval. It will state that the Education Bureau and the local police station have both sent personnel for home visits... There’s no problem, right?
Respondent: I’m giving you special consideration. You understand what I mean, right? The dispatch subsidy provided by our side seems to be quite generous.
Respondent: After you receive the official letter, just send me the list of your relevant staff members and their bank account numbers. We will handle the rest here.

text.name: Proof of Kinship
text.text:
Certificate of Kinship
Self: Cui Dongjian / Born September 15, 1972 / Male
Spouse: Xu Yuanying / Born December 25, 1974 / Female (Deceased)
- Date of Marriage: March 5, 2000
- Date of Death: September 1, 2009
Child: Cui Minghao / Born January 3, 2001 / Male
Child: Cui Xiyuan / Born August 1, 2004 / Female
February 4, 2012
Rongzhou Subdistrict Office

text.name: Unreported New Student Enrollment
text.text:
List of Students Who Did Not Register for New Student Enrollment
Number of Unregistered Students: 4 in total
List of Unregistered Students - Names
(Date of Birth)
- Xu Haojun (Born January 2, 2005) - Jin Fan (Born August 17, 2004) - Huang Renzhe (Born June 25, 2004) - Jin Xiyuan (Born April 3, 2004)

text.name: On the day of new student enrollment
text.text:
Police: On the day of new student registration, you spoke with a staff member from the subdistrict office on the phone, right?
Police: Do you live with your daughter?
Respondent: New student registration? That day...
Respondent: What did my daughter say again... It seemed she said she had a cold? Yes, that should be it.
Respondent: Ah, I remember now.
Respondent: I had been keeping the registration date in mind and later asked her whether she went.
Respondent: We don’t live together. I live nearby and come over to see her whenever I have time.
Respondent: After all...
Respondent: If she stays home alone, she tends to overthink. After a long time, she gets trapped in her emotions and can’t get out.
Respondent: A few days ago, when I went to her home, I happened to receive a call from the subdistrict office.
Respondent: That person asked the same questions as you.
Respondent: I said our granddaughter is doing very well. I will raise my own granddaughter properly. There’s no need for you to worry.
Respondent: I said, Officer.
Respondent: It’s not a big deal if a child doesn’t go to school. Is it necessary to make such a fuss?

text.name: He said he took Si
text.text:
Police: He said he was the one who took Xiyuan away.
Police: Xiyuan’s father turned himself in.
Respondent: Oh my, Officer Quan, how could this happen?
Respondent: You must not believe what he says. I’m going right now
Respondent: to the police station.
Respondent: Everything he said is false.
Respondent: It was me. I was the one who instructed him to do it.
Respondent: It’s all my fault.
Respondent: I’m coming right now. I’ll be there soon. Don’t listen to his nonsense. It’s all my responsibility:

text.name: When Was the Last time You Saw 2
text.text:
Police: When was the last time you saw Xiyuan’s father? Do you two talk often?
Respondent: What about Xiyuan’s father? What does Xiyuan’s disappearance have to do with him?
Respondent: Xiyuan’s father hasn’t been in contact with us for a long time.
Respondent: Ever since the child became like that.
Respondent: Ah... no...
Respondent: I mean, when Xiyuan was seriously ill as a child, he just abandoned her and divorced my daughter. How could he be so heartless?
Respondent: But he definitely wouldn’t secretly take the child away. He’s not that kind of person.
Respondent: Don’t make random suspicions... Nothing will happen.

text.name: You went to pick up Siwon.
text.text:
Police: When you went to pick up Xiyuan, did you see anyone around whom you hadn’t seen before, or anything unusual?
Respondent: It was just as my daughter said.
Respondent: I went to the amusement park to look for Xiyuan, and when I got there, I found no one there...
Respondent: I thought my daughter must have taken the child away.
Respondent: After a while, when my daughter came down and looked at me with a puzzled expression, I knew something had happened.
Respondent: But, Officer, you don’t need to worry too much.
Respondent: I don’t know if my daughter told you that Xiyuan often runs around alone.
Respondent: Don’t be fooled by how anxious my daughter looks. By the evening, this child will run back on her own.
Respondent: You can just go back with peace of mind. I’ll talk to my daughter properly. Honestly, this child really shouldn’t have called the police over nothing.

text.name: Do You Mean Minyoung
text.text:
Police: You mean Ms. Minyoung took Xiyuan home thinking she was her own child, is that right?
Respondent: I asked her what was going on, and Minyoung told me.
Respondent: She heard someone calling Xiyuan’s name, and only after a lot of effort did she finally find her. She searched all the nearby amusement parks.
Respondent: That boy was probably the child’s older brother. Her older brother told her to wait there for him to come back.
Respondent: It must have been when her older brother called her Xiyuan that Minyoung happened to hear it.
Respondent: I don’t know anything else, but I can roughly guess what happened.
Respondent: I guess she must have naturally brought her back, just like any parent picking up a child.
Respondent: And the child acted as if nothing was wrong, calling Minyoung “Auntie, Auntie.”
Respondent: I’m sorry, truly sorry:
Respondent: I should have called the police right away... It wasn’t until the day you came to our home that I suddenly became afraid...
Respondent: My hands wouldn’t stop shaking... I dialed for quite a while, and when I came to my senses, I realized I had called Xiyuan’s father.
Respondent: I was the one who called and asked Xiyuan’s father for help. I told him that Minyoung seemed to have brought someone else’s child home and asked him to help find the child’s parents.
Respondent: I told the child’s father that I would find a way to distract Minyoung, and then he could take the child away.
Respondent: Although my daughter is not in her right mind, she must not become a criminal who abducts a child...
Respondent: ...I, an old woman, truly have no shame.
Respondent: I know that doing this will bring divine punishment. Before Xiyuan’s father turned himself in:
Respondent: I even thought that I could just pretend none of this had happened and act as if I knew nothing...
Respondent: How could I not realize that this child is also the treasure of her parents’ hearts?

text.name: Miss Minyoung Started From
text.text:
Police: Since when did Ms. Minyoung start going out to look for Xiyuan?
Respondent: Her condition suddenly worsened... It should have been because of the elementary school admission notice.
Respondent: In December last year, the subdistrict office sent a piece of mail. I usually open the mail in advance, afraid that there might be something Minyoung shouldn’t see.
Respondent: But when I opened this one and saw the words “admission notice,” it startled me... It was only then that I realized...
Respondent: They had never gone to register.
Respondent: I saw the registration date clearly written on it along with the child’s name... Just looking at it made me feel like I was going crazy... let alone the child’s mother...
Respondent: Oh... I’m sorry, Officer.
Respondent: As a sinner, how could I have the face to complain to you?
Respondent: I’m truly sorry...
Respondent: At that time, I panicked. I accidentally let Minyoung, who was beside me, see it as well.
Respondent: After she saw it, she showed a face full of happiness.
Respondent: I don’t even know how long it had been since I last saw her smile so happily.
Respondent: The registration date written on it was at the end of December. After seeing it, she kept urging me, saying we had to get the school uniform tailored before then.
Respondent: She also said that before school starts, vaccinations were needed and stationery had to be bought. Where has this child gone? Why hasn’t she come back yet?
Respondent: It was from that time on.
Respondent: From that time on, she went to the nearby amusement parks every day to look for Xiyuan.

text.name: It’s all your fault.
text.text:
Police: It’s all your responsibility? What do you mean by that?
Respondent: I’ll tell you the truth.
Respondent: She is dead.
Respondent: Xiyuan... she died a long time ago.
Respondent: She is no longer in this world!

text.name: You seem to know a lot
text.text:
Police: You seem to know quite a lot about Xiyuan’s family.
Respondent: Minghao’s family—I’m indeed quite familiar with them. After all, I’ve known them since they were very young.
Respondent: It’s been... three or four years, I suppose...
Respondent: When Minghao’s family first moved into this residential complex, the first time I saw him, I thought he was an upper-grade elementary school student.
Respondent: Compared to children of the same age, he’s very tall and doesn’t talk much.
Respondent: At that time, Minghao’s mother wanted to buy some school supplies, so I recommended some items used by upper-grade students.
Respondent: I remember Minghao’s mother smiling and saying that Minghao is often misunderstood like that.
Respondent: I don’t know if you’ve met him. Minghao is...
Respondent: Although he is young, he is very mature and steady.
Respondent: Children his age must have many things they want to buy, but every time he stands behind his younger sister and helps her pick the things she likes.

text.name: Your statement that day
text.text:
Police: Part of your statement that day does not match the facts.
Respondent: You’re here again... So you still haven’t found her, right?
Respondent: I’ve also thought carefully about whether any strangers have come here recently... but I really can’t remember.
Respondent: You’re right... In fact, Minghao did come here that day.
Respondent: I’m sorry, I lied. I didn’t think it was particularly important information.
Respondent: Minghao is a good child... I was worried that if I told you, you might form a bad impression of him.
Respondent: I shouldn’t have meddled and caused you trouble. I’m truly sorry.
Respondent: Minghao came over at around 3:30.
Respondent: When he came in, he seemed the same as usual, just a bit anxious. I asked him about it, and he said he had to go back right away and didn’t say anything more.
Respondent: As usual, he picked a bag of candy. I thought to myself: it seems he came to buy candy for his younger sister again today.
Respondent: Xiyuan especially likes that kind of candy—the pink kind that makes your cheeks puff up like a hamster after you put it in your mouth.
Respondent: I’ve told you before that Minghao is a very steady child.
Respondent: But he was very strange that day. He held the candy and squatted in front of the card display counter, lingering there for a long time.
Respondent: Then he came to the cashier and paid for the candy.
Respondent: But he kept his head down and didn’t dare to look at me.
Respondent: I felt something was odd, so after he left, I went to check the counter.
Respondent: ...And then I discovered.
Respondent: One card was missing from the counter.
Respondent: That kid—I thought to myself that next time I saw him, I would definitely teach him a good lesson.
Respondent: But when I thought about how long he had hesitated there...
Respondent: I just felt really uncomfortable inside.

text.name: I heard Siwon often
text.text:
Police: I heard that Xiyuan often comes to this stationery store.
Police: Did Xiyuan’s family come here today? Did Xiyuan come by herself?
Respondent: Today...
Respondent: No, neither Xiyuan nor her older brother came.
Respondent: Um... you’re an officer, right? May I ask what happened?
Respondent: Someone came looking for Xiyuan before as well. Was it Minghao’s mother... Did something happen?
Respondent: Recently, it’s almost always Minghao who comes alone, or Minghao brings Xiyuan with him...
Respondent: When Minghao was little, his mother often brought them here together. I don’t know why we haven’t seen her lately.
Respondent: Is she okay?

text.name: It’s Not Your Fault, Either
text.text:
Police: It’s not your fault, and it’s not Minghao’s fault either.
Police: By the way, Ms. Shen Huijing, I almost forgot to tell you.
Police: Today is your birthday, right? Happy birthday.
Police: I know it may be a bit inappropriate to say this now, but I still think I should tell you.
Police: I went to the stationery store where Minghao often buys candy for Xiyuan. I looked around casually and happened to notice this item.
Police: That day, besides buying candy, he also bought this birthday card. The stationery store owner said Minghao took a long time choosing it.
Police: At the time, I was wondering, there were so many cards there—why did he choose this one in particular?
Police: Seeing you today, I finally understand why.
Respondent: ...Thank you.
Respondent: I always thought... Minghao hated me.
Respondent: I thought he misunderstood me... I never intended to replace his mother’s position...
Respondent: How could I be so foolish...
Respondent: Knowing full well that he had suffered so much...
Respondent: Officer Quan,
Respondent: How is Xiyuan’s mother now?

text.name: To a fourth-grade in elementary
text.text:
Police: For a fourth-grade elementary school child, silence is truly too heavy, yet he has kept enduring it.
Police: I really wanted to ease his psychological burden, so I asked everyone I could find—the nearby residents, passersby, shop owners...
Police: There is a place... right behind the flower bed.
Police: Standing there, you can see the amusement park through a small gap, and it’s not easy for Minghao to notice.
Police: You stood there watching them every time, didn’t you?
Respondent: In the amusement park, there are some children about the same age as Xiyuan.
Respondent: When we went to the amusement park, the parents of those children often gathered together and whispered.
Respondent: Minghao must have heard it too.
Respondent: Because Xiyuan always calls me mom, it does easily cause misunderstandings.
Respondent: I can understand why Minghao would dislike me, so I didn’t feel too hurt because of it.
Respondent: It was probably a few weeks ago. Minghao told me not to go near them and to stay away. Then, while I was wandering around nearby, I discovered that place.
Respondent: Minghao...
Respondent: He must really hate that I did this... but...
Respondent: I...
Respondent: Although I am not his mother, but...
Respondent: I promised Yuanying that I would protect them well.
Respondent: I never expected it to turn out like this in the end.
Respondent: It really was only for a short while...
Respondent: Because standing on tiptoe all the time was too exhausting, I just rested for a short while...

text.name: What about your son—was he also
text.text:
Police: What about your son? Did he also disappear? I remember you went to the amusement park together, right?
Respondent: Minghao was right there the whole time, but he said he didn’t see where Xiyuan ran off to either.
Respondent: I don’t know how this could have happened...
Respondent: I questioned him for a long time, trying to get some clues from him... Maybe I pushed him too hard...
Respondent: The one who lost Xiyuan was clearly me...
Respondent: I’m sorry to them—to Xiyuan and Minghao... It’s all my fault.
Respondent: Could you please not question Minghao?
Respondent: He won’t say anything.

text.name: As I Understand, You Were
text.text:
Police: As far as I know, you did not go to the amusement park that day.
Respondent: I know you’re worried that Minghao will blame himself, but you shouldn’t think that way.
Respondent: How did you know?
Respondent: I already told him not to say anything...
Respondent: I told Minghao that it’s okay not to say anything...
Respondent: Xiyuan’s disappearance is not his fault.
Respondent: He thinks it happened because he didn’t want to stay with me.
Respondent: I was the one who failed to keep an eye on Xiyuan. It’s all my fault...
Respondent: I clearly told him that I was the one who lost Xiyuan.

text.name: How do you feel about kind
text.text:
Police: What do you think about what the kindergarten teacher said?
Respondent: I truly... am very grateful.
Respondent: I never expected her to care so much about us. Xiyuan always says...
Respondent: Mom is the most pitiful person in the world.
Respondent: When it’s just the two of us, she often says that to me... I think I now somewhat understand what she meant.
Respondent: Xiyuan thinks mom is the most pitiful person in the world.
Respondent: But if Xiyuan cries:
Respondent: The people around her will think Xiyuan is pitiful and come to comfort her...
Respondent: Then Xiyuan would become more pitiful than mom.
Respondent: She thinks that shouldn’t happen. That seems to be what she was thinking...
Respondent: Xiyuan is a sensible child.
Respondent: At such a young age, she has already learned to weigh emotions.
Respondent: It’s truly... heartbreaking.

text.name: When was the last time you saw her?
text.text:
Police: When was the last time you saw Xiyuan at the amusement park?
Respondent: 3:33.
Respondent: Officer, Xiyuan has been missing for three hours.
Respondent: Xiyuan is only seven years old. I’ve searched everywhere she could possibly go by herself.
Respondent: What should we do now?
Respondent: My mind is filled with all kinds of terrible imaginations... I can’t shake them off...

text.name: Why do you remem
text.text:
Police: Why do you remember the time so precisely?
Respondent: There’s a call record on my phone.
Respondent: When I go out with the children, I never leave them alone to go somewhere else.
Respondent: But... I received a phone call.
Respondent: Usually, hardly anyone calls me in the afternoon.
Respondent: So I might have been a bit flustered at that moment.
Respondent: I wanted to find a quieter place to take the call,
Respondent: so I went into the corridor of a nearby building...
Respondent: The call only lasted five minutes, and I looked away for less than five minutes.
Respondent: Because the call wasn’t finished, I came back, but by then Xiyuan was already gone.

text.name: Everything Auntie said
text.text:
Police: What Auntie said is all true, right? You must not lie.
Respondent: Auntie told me that sometimes people need kind lies rather than the truth.
Respondent: She said that lying itself isn’t bad—only bad lies are bad.
Respondent: Mom said she would watch over us from heaven. She told me that even if she passed away, she would protect us from the sky.
Respondent: But...
Respondent: She was lying. There is no such thing as heaven in this world.
Respondent: Xiyuan still doesn’t know that mom lied.
Respondent: She still foolishly believes what mom said...
Respondent: If mom is a liar,
Respondent: then is she also a bad person?

text.name: It’s not your fault, Myeongho, and
text.text:
Police: It’s not your fault, Minghao. And it’s not anyone in your family’s fault either.
Respondent: I was the one who told Auntie not to come to the amusement park.
Respondent: I told her that I wanted to go with Xiyuan alone and asked her to stay away from us.
Respondent: That’s why this happened. It’s all my fault. I was the one who told her not to come.
Respondent: Because if we were all at the amusement park,
Respondent: it would look like a family...
Respondent: Mom would see from heaven that Xiyuan calls Auntie “mom.”
Respondent: I don’t believe she is really watching us from heaven. I know she was lying.
Respondent: But...
Respondent: I don’t want mom to be sad.
Respondent: It’s not Auntie’s fault.
Respondent: I was the one who told her not to come.

text.name: Then listen to me.
text.text:
Police: Then listen to me, okay? You can try to recall carefully.
Police: At that time, did you see anyone nearby whom you hadn’t seen before? I heard that you were all at the amusement park.
Police: Mom, Xiyuan, and Minghao, right?
Respondent: ...Mm... yes.
Respondent: We... were all together.

text.name: If you don’t want to say it, that’s fine
text.text:
Police: It’s okay if you don’t want to talk. I’ll wait for you.
Police: But Minghao, if you’re ready to say it,
Police: you must tell me. Can you promise me?
Respondent: ................

text.name: Can you tell me you
text.text:
Police: Can you tell me what happened the last time you saw Xiyuan?
Respondent: ...Before...
Respondent: When we went home together, we would go to the stationery store to buy candy for Xiyuan.
Respondent: But because Auntie hasn’t been going to the amusement park with us recently, Xiyuan hadn’t had any candy for several days.
Respondent: I told Xiyuan to stay there and not move, then I ran to the stationery store to buy candy for her.
Respondent: The stationery store is right next to the amusement park. You just have to climb a flight of stairs. It’s really very close.
Respondent: I was only gone for a short while. I ran there.
Respondent: But Xiyuan...
Respondent: ...was gone.
Respondent: I called her many times...
Respondent: But she didn’t come. Only Auntie came over.
Respondent: Auntie told me... not to tell anyone, not to say that Auntie wasn’t with us.
Respondent: She told me not to say anything...
Respondent: Like the monkeys we saw at the temple...

text.name: If I tell you
text.text:
Police: What if I tell you that you don’t need to lie now?
Police: What if I tell you that your lie is a bad lie and will hurt Auntie and Xiyuan even more?
Respondent: Why is it a bad lie if I don’t say anything?
Respondent: If I say it...
Respondent: If I tell the truth...
Respondent: It will make Auntie look like a bad person.
Respondent: But Auntie is a good person.
Respondent: Actually, it’s because of me...
Respondent: It’s all my fault.

text.name: Thank you for telling me
text.text:
Police: Thank you for telling me, Minghao.
Police: By the way, Minghao, I heard you’re in fifth grade in elementary school now, right?
Police: You’re already this tall in fifth grade. You must have inherited your mom’s genes. You even look quite like your mom. You must be very popular at school, right?
Respondent: ...Do I look like her?
Respondent: Do I really...
Respondent: look like her?

text.name: About Siwon in kind
text.text:
Police: Is there anything you want to say about Xiyuan’s life in kindergarten?
Respondent: I’ve already said everything else on the phone.
Respondent: She still hasn’t been found? How could something like this happen in broad daylight? And inside the residential complex...
Respondent: I heard that at the time, Xiyuan’s mother and older brother were both there. Did they really not see anything?
Respondent: Xiyuan... I don’t know whether saying this will help you.
Respondent: Since you said I can say anything, then I’ll say it.
Respondent: Xiyuan has always had a lively and cheerful personality.
Respondent: When I first met her last year, she wasn’t shy at all. She even startled several of us teachers.
Respondent: At first, I thought she was just easygoing.
Respondent: Since her mom is gone, most of the time it was her older brother who came to pick her up, but I never saw her look for her mom.
Respondent: If you ask whether she had any problems... none at all. She had no problems whatsoever.
Respondent: It’s just...
Respondent: I never saw her cry, nor did I ever see her get angry or throw a tantrum... Do you understand what I mean?
Respondent: I often told myself that a child like her needs even more of my attention, and that I must take even more careful care of her.
Respondent: Because I always felt... her smile was like a bubble under the sunlight. It looks beautiful, but it would burst with just the slightest touch.
Respondent: Do you understand that feeling?

text.name: Okay, I Understand
text.text:
Police: Alright, I understand. Please describe again the process of how you saw Xiyuan and then took her away.
Respondent: After graduating from the normal university, I worked as an English teacher at a middle school.
Respondent: After divorcing my wife, for various reasons... I resigned from my job at the school. Sometimes I worked as an instructor at training centers, and sometimes I did some private tutoring.
Respondent: It’s just... these jobs didn’t provide stable income... so I was short on money... I’m sorry:
Respondent: I went to that amusement park intending to take away a child who was alone.
Respondent: I observed nearby for more than half an hour. I saw a little girl playing there alone, so I deceived her and took her away...
Respondent: But after bringing her back, I suddenly became afraid and didn’t know how to ask her parents for ransom.
Respondent: So...
Respondent: I sent her back. That’s what happened.

text.name: You’re Not Reflecting
text.text:
Police: You are not reflecting. You are lying.
Police: When Xiyuan went missing, who was around, what were they wearing, which direction did you flee from—
Police: You can’t answer any of these questions.
Police: Mr. Jin Kangshi:
Police: You say you are the one who kidnapped the child.
Police: Is it possible that you are actually depriving Ms. Minyoung of the chance to atone and be forgiven?
Police: You can bear the punishment for her now, but what about after she recovers?
Police: At that time, she will have to face her own self-blame and guilt!
Police: Can you bear that for her?
Police: Your mother-in-law is in the room next door. She has already told me everything.
Police: In order to protect her son-in-law, she had no choice but to report her own biological daughter. Think about how she must feel right now.
Police: I know that you have been covering Ms. Song Minyoung’s rehabilitation treatment expenses under the name of child support.
Police: Now I ask you to take one more step back and stand behind her to support her.
Police: If Ms. Minyoung is sent for treatment and supervision, it will be a very long battle.
Respondent: ...Officer Quan.
Respondent: Do you think it’s possible that I made a mistake with the very first step?
Respondent: ...The name Xiyuan...
Respondent: Could it be that everything turned out this way because I gave her the wrong name...?

text.name: You and Siwon’s Mom
text.text:
Police: When did you and Xiyuan’s mother separate?
Respondent: Our divorce... was five or six years ago.
Respondent: Am I very cruel? Abandoning my wife like that and leaving her to face the pain alone.
Respondent: But at that time, I thought separating was the best choice for both of us.
Respondent: I felt we couldn’t continue like this, so I found myself an excuse to escape from everything.
Respondent: I could no longer face her hollow eyes, because I knew nothing could ever fill that emptiness again.
Respondent: If we could have held each other and cried, comforted one another, and lived our days together, how wonderful that would have been.
Respondent: But I couldn’t spend my whole life watching her struggle in a swamp of emptiness.
Respondent: One day, I finally realized that compared to the trauma already suffered, what was even more painful was having someone by your side constantly reminding you of that trauma.
Respondent: From that day on, we decided to live our separate lives.
Respondent: We chose to avoid this pain.
Respondent: From then on, we made a clean break.
Respondent: Completely locking the doors to each other’s hearts.

text.name: You’re here to turn yourself in.
text.text:
Police: Did you come to turn yourself in?
Respondent: Yes, I turned myself in. I did it.
Respondent: You’re looking for a little girl, right? The one who went missing at the amusement park three days ago.
Respondent: I was the one who took her away. I am the criminal.
Respondent: I’m sorry. I deserve to die.
Respondent: I desperately needed money, so...
Respondent: I’m sorry.

text.name: What do you mean, a cold case?
text.text:
Police: What did you say? An unsolved case? No, Xiyuan’s father, we can’t do that.
Respondent: Xiyuan’s disappearance has now been officially filed as a case, right?
Respondent: That means Xiyuan is registered in the system as a missing child, correct?
Respondent: That’s good. That’s enough.
Respondent: Officer Quan...
Respondent: I beg you.
Respondent: Please stop looking for Xiyuan.
Respondent: Don’t ask where Xiyuan is anymore.
Respondent: Let her live forever in some place where her mother can never find her.
Respondent: Forever... okay?
Respondent: Xiyuan just went missing while playing at the amusement park. That’s all. This is a perfect disappearance case—no witnesses and no suspects.
Respondent: Please... let this case... remain an unsolved case forever.
Respondent: I kneel and beg you, okay?

text.name: Why Did You turn yourself in
text.text:
Police: Why did you turn yourself in?
Police: The victim’s parents have not reported Mr. Jin Kangshi.
Police: You turning yourself in can’t just be about taking Ms. Minyoung’s place to accept punishment, right?
Respondent: I heard that Xiyuan’s mother reported the case to the police station.
Respondent: When my mother-in-law told me about it, although I was worried about Minyoung’s condition, I also felt a bit relieved.
Respondent: Ever since we divorced.
Respondent: She underwent a long period of treatment. You must have heard about that too, right?
Respondent: I should have sought help when she started going out to look for Xiyuan more and more frequently—no, I should have done it right after that incident happened...
Respondent: The day Minyoung was discharged from the hospital happened to be Xiyuan’s birthday.
Respondent: We went to the cemetery to see her. My wife silently stroked the grave... In her eyes, I could no longer see even a trace of hope.
Respondent: Her life seemed to have stopped on the day Xiyuan left, like the hands of a clock spinning in place.
Respondent: I think... she may have already given up on her own life.
Respondent: Looking at her despairing face, I doubted whether she could ever truly recover.
Respondent: Perhaps that is...
Respondent: why when I heard she had started going out to look for Xiyuan again, I suddenly felt relieved.
Respondent: It seemed she still wanted to live. If she kept struggling like this, maybe... she could stand up again.
Respondent: Maybe Minyoung reported the case with that kind of mindset as well.
Respondent: Turning Xiyuan into a child who is forever missing is better than accepting the fact that she is already dead.
Respondent: Perhaps she thought that this missing registration form could bring Xiyuan back to life once more.
Respondent: Like a drowning person clutching at a straw.
Respondent: ...I know my thoughts are foolish, but it was this foolish thought that gave me courage.
Respondent: I want to ask you...
Respondent: Let Xiyuan’s disappearance remain an unsolved case forever, okay?
Respondent: Let Xiyuan...
Respondent: Please...
Respondent: Let Xiyuan...
Respondent: live forever somewhere.

text.name: Why Have You Only Come Now
text.text:
Police: Why haven’t you reported it until now?
Respondent: 108 days.
Respondent: Xiyuan was by our side, breathing with us, for a total of 108 days.
Respondent: In those days... even just once...
Respondent: If we could hold her in our arms, kiss her cheeks, and feel her body temperature.
Respondent: Even if we could just hear her cry...
Respondent: Would that have made it... a little easier to bear?
Respondent: Xiyuan’s mother’s chest was still flowing with breast milk that had no owner.
Respondent: The place where Xiyuan once lay still retained her body warmth... lingering for a long time.
Respondent: How could I... how could I personally...
Respondent: I kept thinking.
Respondent: It must be because of the name...
Respondent: It was the name.
Respondent: I shouldn’t have given her that name. I blamed myself for a long time because of it.
Respondent: I originally named her that in the hope that she would be as strong as a rhinoceros, but instead she left alone like a rhinoceros horn...
Respondent: Severing all ties and afflictions.
Respondent: With no attachment and no longing, like a gust of wind...

text.name: Siwon’s name has
text.text:
Police: Does Xiyuan’s name have any special meaning?
Respondent: Xiyuan was born at the 23rd week of my wife’s pregnancy. Her birth weight was less than 700 grams.
Respondent: After the surgery, before my wife and Xiyuan were transferred to the intensive care unit, a nurse loudly called my name.
Respondent: Although it was only for a few brief seconds, I saw her.
Respondent: She looked so small, like a translucent Thumbelina wrapped in red tulip petals...
Respondent: I didn’t dare to breathe for a moment, afraid that she would be blown away like a dandelion seed.
Respondent: The nurse asked me if I saw clearly, but I couldn’t see anything clearly...
Respondent: Tears kept blurring my vision, preventing me from engraving her appearance into my eyes.
Respondent: After that hurried glimpse, do you know what the first thing I did was?
Respondent: Birth registration.
Respondent: I ran all the way from the hospital to the subdistrict office. Xiyuan.
Respondent: Xi as in rhinoceros, Yuan as in origin. Isn’t it a very special name?
Respondent: I hoped she would be as strong as a rhinoceros... so I gave her this name.
Respondent: I used all my strength to write her name stroke by stroke on the paper.
Respondent: I hoped that this document bearing her name:
Respondent: would become resilient roots allowing her to take deep root in this world.
Respondent: would become a huge anchor allowing her soul to moor by our side.

text.name: Where Is Siwon Now
text.text:
Police: Where is Xiyuan now?
Respondent: That child is now with her family.
Respondent: After feeding her dinner, I took her back.
Respondent: We walked to the place where I first saw that girl, near the amusement park. After we got there, she recognized the way home.
Respondent: I rang the doorbell and waited at the gate for her parents to come out.
Respondent: In that brief moment,
Respondent: I was still wondering whether I should just abandon her and run away.
Respondent: I am such a useless person. I know that no matter what, I should never have kidnapped a child. I truly regret it. I was so foolish.
Respondent: The child’s father...
Respondent: After he came out, he hugged the child and cried at the door. I immediately knelt down and apologized to him...
Respondent: I never expected that he would actually...
Respondent: kneel in front of me.
Respondent: and say thank you...
Respondent: Thank me for bringing the child back safely...
Respondent: I’m sorry. I am willing to accept punishment.
Respondent: I know that even if I am punished, it cannot lessen the pain they suffered, but I am willing to spend the rest of my life reflecting on myself.

text.name: It’s okay, I’ll ask again.
text.text:
Police: It’s okay. Let me ask again—was there anything different from usual in Xiyuan’s schedule today?
Respondent: No... it was the same as usual.
Respondent: She goes to kindergarten from Monday to Friday. On weekends, she usually goes to the amusement park with her family.
Respondent: There are two amusement parks inside the residential complex. She takes turns going to play at them.
Respondent: Sometimes I go with them as well. If it’s an amusement park that’s inconvenient for a wheelchair, I let Huijing take the children there by herself...
Respondent: I remember now.
Respondent: Recently, they seemed to have been going to the same amusement park. Huijing said they were going to that one today as well... The children insisted on going there to play...
Respondent: If they had gone to a different amusement park, maybe this wouldn’t have happened.
Respondent: On the way back from the amusement park, sometimes they would stop by the stationery store in front of the residential complex.
Respondent: That stationery store is called Apollo.
Respondent: Xiyuan really likes the candy there.

text.name: Myeongho also and Siwon
text.text:
Police: Is Minghao the same as Xiyuan?
Police: The process of acceptance couldn’t have been that easy, right?
Respondent: There is a waterfront park next to our residential complex. When your police station investigated the area nearby, you should have been there.
Respondent: In the park, there are several weeping willows swaying gently like flowing water, looking very lonely.
Respondent: Last year, when Minghao, Huipin, and I went for a walk in the park, I suddenly felt that Minghao was very much like those weeping willows.
Respondent: Although he seems to sway with the wind, deep inside he is especially profound and firm.
Respondent: For children... actually, for adults like me as well,
Respondent: losing a family member is like experiencing the collapse of one’s world.
Respondent: The process of rebuilding that collapsed world must take a long time.
Respondent: But our Minghao overcame it in his own way.
Respondent: Whenever Minghao goes out, he always holds something in his hand. Have you noticed?

text.name: You mean the umbrella
text.text:
Police: You’re talking about an umbrella, right?
Respondent: Yes, that’s right.
Respondent: Whether he goes to school or out to play, as long as he leaves the house, he always holds an umbrella.
Respondent: He started doing this after my wife passed away.
Respondent: When my wife was still in the hospital bed, she said some things to Minghao.
Respondent: She made an agreement with Minghao. She said that mom would go to heaven first to protect you.
Respondent: At that time, Minghao sat far away and didn’t say a word, but I remember he let out a soft sigh.
Respondent: I think he might have wanted to tell his mom that there is no such thing as heaven in this world, and that mom should stay by our side to protect us.
Respondent: But he didn’t say it out loud.
Respondent: After my wife passed away, it was only after a long time that I noticed Minghao always held an umbrella whenever he went out.
Respondent: Only then did I remember what exactly the agreement between my wife and Minghao was.
Respondent: Mom didn’t lie to you, okay? From now on, when it rains, mom can’t come to pick you up...
Respondent: If one day it rains and you forget to bring an umbrella, I will make the rain stop, okay?

text.name: Ms. Shin Hui-jing is
text.text:
Police: From what age did Ms. Shen Huijing start taking care of Xiyuan?
Respondent: It’s been many years. The first time she came was when Xiyuan was four years old.
Respondent: During the time when my wife passed away, I felt like the sky had collapsed. I didn’t know how to take care of the children.
Respondent: Thanks to Huijing, she helped me tremendously.
Respondent: Recently, I think people call it a nanny, right?
Respondent: She was the nanny I hired to help take care of the children.
Respondent: Since my wife began her hospitalization, she came to our home every day to look after the children. The children also liked her very much.
Respondent: After my wife suddenly passed away, it was also because of her that the children were able to get through that difficult time smoothly.
Respondent: Especially Xiyuan—she was very close to Huijing and always called her mom.
Respondent: I am truly very grateful to her—
Respondent: I never expected something like this to happen. It seems I relied on her too much.
Respondent: After all... she is not family...

text.name: Is Siwon Okay Now
text.text:
Police: Is Xiyuan okay now?
Respondent: She said she had a great time playing at Auntie’s home.
Respondent: Later, she told Auntie that she missed her dad, so she was sent back...
Respondent: I’m truly sorry. I should have contacted you earlier.
Respondent: I was only thinking about myself... even though I knew you were still looking for the child...
Respondent: That person returned the child three days after Xiyuan went missing, but I didn’t ask anything.
Respondent: You may find it strange when I say this, but... other than thanking him, I didn’t know what else to say.
Respondent: Even if you asked me to kowtow a hundred times... I would do it without hesitation.
Respondent: As long as Xiyuan came back safe and sound...
Respondent: I think that’s enough.
Respondent: Xiyuan...
Respondent: has suffered a lot since she was little...
Respondent: Yet I let her be hurt once again... I am an incompetent father.
Respondent: That person...
Respondent: Did he turn himself in?

text.name: Is there anything near the playground
text.text:
Police: Are there any places near the amusement park that she often goes to? For example, somewhere familiar that she could find on her own.
Respondent: Do you think she wandered off by herself? Do you take her for a three-year-old child?
Respondent: Is it possible that she was abducted?
Respondent: Hurry up and send people to look for her! Don’t waste time here!
Respondent: What if she was taken by criminals? If you don’t act now, it will be too late!
Respondent: I don’t even know whether Xiyuan is safe right now...
Respondent: And you still have the leisure to sit here and ask me where she went by herself?
Respondent: Is this how you police handle cases?!
Respondent: ...Damn it.
Respondent: ...I’m sorry.
